$comment: The generated artifacts whose commit-binding is gated, and the rule that makes that binding CHECKABLE (TASK-S0-O1). Data, not code: governing one more artifact is an edit here. Read `evidence-binding.ts` first -- it states why `sourceCommit === HEAD` is the wrong invariant and what replaces it.
$whyNotEqualsHead: An artifact is written into the working tree at HEAD = X; the commit that lands it is X+1. A committed artifact therefore ALWAYS stamps its own parent, and no generator can do better -- the commit it 'should' name does not exist while the file is being written. `packages/tooling/src/quality/git.ts` says so in `headCommit()`'s own doc comment and routes it to the owner as D1. A gate spelled `sourceCommit === HEAD` is red on every commit that lands a regeneration, which is the one commit where the artifact is most correct, so it trains people to ignore it. The question that actually matters is ORDERING: did anything the artifact is generated FROM change after the artifact was stamped? That is what this gate asks.
$howInputsAreMatched: Each artifact declares its own `generatedFrom` globs. They are handed to `git log <sourceCommit>..HEAD -- :(glob)<pattern>` unchanged, so git does the pathspec matching and this repository gains no second glob implementation. A `#fragment` suffix (`package.json#exports`) and a trailing ` (report)` annotation are stripped first; both name a file, not a path pattern.
$generatedOutputsComment: Paths that are OUTPUTS of the same regeneration cycle. A commit that lands a regeneration touches all of them at once, so a later stamp on one of them is not evidence that an earlier one is stale -- they are compared by stamp (rule 3) or, where they carry no stamp, deliberately not compared at all. Listing a genuine SOURCE here would blind the gate, so every entry must be something a generator writes.
